newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo's op. profit rises 60 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Volvo's op. profit rises 60 pct in Q1.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Wednesday that its operating income for the three months ending March 31 rose 60 percent to 1.89 billion crowns ($246.7 million) against 1.18 billion crowns a year earlier.
This included a 200 million crown gain from currency movement.

Volvo said its pre-tax profit for the first quarter of 1997 rose to 5.25 billion crowns, which included a capital gain of 3.03 billion crowns from the sale of shares in drinks group Pripps Ringnes as part of its divestment programme.
($ = 7.661 Swedish Crowns)
The markets had been expecting a pre-tax profit of 5.01 billion crowns in the first quarter.
The company said Volvo Car showed a turnaround from a loss of 191 million crowns in the first quarter of 1996 to a profit in the first three months of 1997 of 1.07 billion crowns.
It said this was due to a larger volume of business and higher margins. It was also helped to a certain degree by the favourable effect of currency movements.
It said Volvo Car net sales rose 18 percent and it increased its sales and share in most European markets. This was due largely to higher sales of the S40 and V40 models.
It said that the new Volvo S70 and V70 models had also contributed to the sales increases.
It said the total number of Volvo cars registered in Germany, Spain and the Netherlands rose by 30 percent compared with the year-earlier period.

The company also said that marketing of the S70 and the V70 had begun in North America during the latter part of the quarter. Sales in Japan had continued to rise although the company's share of the market had declined.

The company said the world market for cars rose by about one percent in the first quarter thanks to a rise in sales in Japan although the Japanese market was expected to level off during the rest of the year as higher taxes hit in April.
It said demand in Europe and North America was expected to be around the same for the full year 1997 as it was in 1996.
The Volvo TruckS business showed a fall in operating income to 304 million crowns from 731 million crowns due to a smaller volume of sales and lower margins in Europe.
It said the total market for heavy trucks in Europe and the U.S. fell during the early part of the year, although there were signs of a gradual recovery in the U.S. market.
"The world market for heavy trucks in 1997 is expected to be smaller than in 1996, mainly due to weaker demand in Europe," the company said.
It delivered 14,500 medium-heavy and heavy trucks in the first quarter, 13 percent less than in Q1 1996.
Deliveries in Europe fell 22 percent, were unchanged in North America and rose three percent in South America.
Volvo Buses operating income rose to 87 million crowns from 69 million crowns due to larger business volumes and favourable exchange rates.

It said that its Volvo Construction Equipment business boosted operating income to 309 million crowns from 273 million due to a favourable U.S. dollar and the contribution from the newly-bought Champion Road Machinery Ltd.
-- Patrick Lannin, Stockholm newsroom +46 8 700 1006
